## Correct calls and misses

The 1H conversion recovered to ~50% (vs. 27% in 2019 chop) and daily
accuracy hit 79% on both coins. The system did real work in the
trending parts of the cycle. The losses tell two stories:

### Story 1 — chase entries near and into the ATH

Of the 15 BTC losers, **nine are continuation longs at progressively
higher prices through the bull cycle**, every one of them with price
already extended near the recent high:

| Date       | Entry  | Approx prior swing low | Extension above swing low |
| ---------- | ------ | ---------------------- | ------------------------- |
| 2020-11-09 | 15549  | ~10000 (Oct)           | +55%                      |
| 2020-12-07 | 19318  | ~13000 (Nov)           | +49%                      |
| 2020-12-21 | 23679  | ~16000 (Dec)           | +48%                      |
| 2021-01-04 | 32844  | ~16000 (Dec)           | +105%                     |
| 2021-03-15 | 59404  | ~30000 (Jan)           | +98%                      |
| 2021-05-03 | 57408  | ~50000 (Apr pullback)  | +15%                      |
| 2021-08-16 | 47547  | ~30000 (Jul)           | +58%                      |
| 2021-10-18 | 62461  | ~40000 (Sep)           | +56%                      |
| 2021-11-08 | 64999  | ~58000 (Oct pullback)  | +12%                      |

ETH repeats it: $456 / $552 / $1457 / $1742 / $3909 / $3312 / $4132 /
$4688 / $4674 — the same chase profile up the same cycle.

In every case the entry is in the lower half of the retracement
zone of the impulse leg (price still near the high). The Phase 1
`retracement_entry_zones` section explicitly says "75% is minimum,
86% is optimal, 50% is NEVER an entry" — but it never specifies *what
leg* the percentage is measured against. Without a leg-identification
rule, the engine effectively re-anchors the leg every week and finds a
"fresh 75% retracement" right at the high.

### Story 2 — post-flush counter-shorts (already covered)

The May 2021 crash produced BTC short entries at 05-24 ($35191) and
05-31 ($35313), and ETH at the same dates. These are the same
post-climax shorts that iter 4's `post_climax_cooldown` already
addresses — the May 2021 daily candle on the crash day exceeds 4×
20-day ATR. No new theory needed; this pattern is already covered.

## What changed and why

**One concrete theory improvement:** added two new subsections under
`retracement_entry_zones` in `docs/technical.yaml`:

1. **`impulse_leg_identification`** — defines the current impulse leg
   as the leg between the most recent confirmed daily swing low and
   swing high that bracket the most recent break of structure on the
   daily timeframe. Confirms a swing point only after three quiet
   daily closes. The leg is locked until either a fresh BOS in the
   bias direction extends it, or a counter-bias BOS invalidates it.
   An explicit `do_not_re_anchor_per_week` rule prohibits the
   re-anchoring pathology.

2. **`chase_prevention_rule`** — once the impulse leg is identified,
   a fresh entry is allowed ONLY when current price is inside the
   75-86-90% retracement zone of that leg. If price is in the 0-50%
   zone — i.e., still extended near the impulse high (for longs) or
   low (for shorts) — NO fresh entry is allowed regardless of any
   other signal. Includes a `how_to_apply` block specifying the
   weekly check sequence (chase test before 4H setup), a
   relationship_to_existing_rules note tying it to
   `market_phase_discipline` and clarifying it is the slower-grind
   cousin of `post_climax_cooldown`, and a `note_for_engines` block
   specifying the per-coin per-direction `impulse_leg` state the
   engine must persist (origin/terminal swing price + date).

### Why this is the right theory improvement for 2020-2021

The dominant trade-level loss bucket is chase entries: nine of fifteen
BTC losers and at least nine of fourteen ETH losers are entries in
the 0-30% retracement zone of an existing extended impulse leg. The
Phase 1 `retracement_entry_zones` already declared 75-86% as the only
valid entry band — but a backtest engine (or a careless reader) can
ignore the requirement entirely if no rule says *which* leg the
percentage is measured against. This iteration adds that missing
rule and the explicit chase-prevention test.

It does NOT replace `re_entry_discipline` (iter 3, the no-pyramiding
rule) or `post_climax_cooldown` (iter 4, the climax-flag suspension).
The three rules now stack:

- Chase prevention catches slow-grind extensions (this iter).
- Climax cooldown catches single-candle regime inversions (iter 4).
- Re-entry discipline catches pyramiding into the same impulse (iter 3).

Each rule fires on a different failure mode and they are compatible.

## 4H/1H execution notes

- The 14 winning entries on each coin are clustered in the
  *post-pullback* segments of the cycle: late 2020 dip-buys after
  the September 2020 retracement, the February 2021 dip, the July
  2021 dip, the September 2021 dip, and the December 2021
  intermediate bounce. The model works well at retracement-buy
  conditions — it just was not gated against the chase entries in
  between.
- Daily accuracy at 79% remains strong; the leak is not at the bias
  layer.
- The double-top in November 2021 produced a 2021-12-20 BTC short
  that was stopped out — this is a lower-conviction failure mode
  that none of the iter 1-5 rules currently address (it's a
  bottom-fishing short rather than a top-chasing long). Carry to
  later iterations.

## Open questions for later iterations

1. **Bottom-fishing shorts at the start of a downtrend** (BTC
   2021-12-20). Symmetric to the top-chasing long pattern but
   directionally inverted. The chase-prevention rule from this iter
   handles top-chasing longs cleanly; a parallel "no fresh shorts
   inside the upper half of the impulse leg" rule may be needed for
   the bear side. Today's rule is symmetric in language but the
   2021-12-20 short was at a moderate retracement level, not at the
   high — so this is a different failure mode.
2. **The "weekly bias still long while 4H/daily are flipping short"
   transition window** at cycle peaks (Oct-Nov 2021). Lag of weekly
   MA produces stale long bias even when daily structure is breaking.
   Carry to later iterations.
